prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper) intakes emergency-medical calls, creates incident records, triages/dispatches, coordinates jurisdictions, checks coverage, escalates readiness gaps, and preserves original reports alongside clarifications. Jurisdictions retain ownership/local-policy responsibility. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur) establishes/verifies location before medical details; captures callback, symptoms/onset/source, immediate hazards/access; produces Caller Location Correction Slip; updates records with clarifications before dispatch finalization. Clinical triage follows symptom/location/hazard capture; records never replace reassessment. Computer Aided Dispatch Console supports assessment/dispatch/location checking; verify data currency. Ambulance Coordination Platform shares incidents/assignments/coverage/availability/status. Ambulance Unit 417 joins response pool upon assignment. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield) reviews uncertainty/conflicts/deterioration, directs focused clarification without delaying urgent response, escalates ambiguous/severe cases to Regional Medical Director when time permits, and sends Pediatric Acuity Note. Priority reflects life threat, care time-sensitivity, deterioration/delay harm; immediate threats require highest available priority/prompt dispatch. Regional Medical Director sets clinical policy/delegation limits, not operational dispatch authority. Paramedic Crew assesses/treats within protocols/scope, seeks beyond-authority guidance, reports access/readiness concerns. Shift Commander (Sundial) manages continuity/surge/conflicts/readiness/repositioning/coverage; escalates beyond-center decisions to jurisdictional leadership without overriding clinical policy/crew judgment. Hospital Liaison Desk (Kestrel) confirms capabilities/contact pathways/preference compatibility, coordinates capacity/destinations, records constraints in incident notes, produces Bedside Arrival Receipt after confirmed ambulance arrival, shares current information without delaying intake. Emergency Department communicates receiving considerations; Riverside Trauma Center suitability/availability follows protocols. Jurisdictions review zone boundaries after road/population/agreement changes. Destination routes follow clinical/access constraints; dispatch checks travel/restrictions/weather/closures; crews verify constrained routes. North Gate Status Board produces North Approach Queue Snapshot; South Gate Status Board displays restrictions; check both each shift/change. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) manages Regional Radio Network; check channels/backups/weak-area coverage each shift. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay) monitors defects/service/availability; produces Battery Swap Voucher. Readiness checks: staffing/communications/supplies/fuel/condition/restrictions; reassess after incidents/interruptions/access changes. Data Quality Officer (Pebble) monitors completeness/consistency/duplicates/recurring

New part:
S089: Data Quality Officer flags data defects for review but does not independently change a clinical priority.
S090: Computer Aided Dispatch Console presents the current incident details and assigned priority to authorized dispatch staff.
S091: Ambulance Coordination Platform uses the recorded priority alongside unit availability and operational constraints when coordinating response resources.
S092: Radio Coordinator communicates dispatch instructions and priority changes over Regional Radio Network.
S093: Paramedic Crew reports material changes in patient condition so that the incident can be reassessed promptly.
S094: Ambulance Unit 417 follows the active dispatch instructions and requests clarification when the incident details do not support safe response.
S095: Emergency Department may provide operationally relevant capacity information, while clinical triage remains governed by approved regional protocols.
S096: Riverside Trauma Center is considered for destination coordination when the patient's needs and current clinical guidance support that option.
S097: Shift Commander is notified when competing high-priority incidents exceed available response capacity or require an operational exception.
S098: Data Quality Officer reviews whether priority changes and their supporting rationale are recorded consistently for later assessment.
S099: Regional Dispatch Center preserves the original caller report alongside subsequent clarifications so responders can distinguish confirmed details from estimates.
S100: Triage Supervisor reviews significant disagreements about urgency and records the basis for the final operational priority.
S101: Resource selection begins after the operational priority and essential response requirements have been confirmed.
S102: The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents units whose reported status and capabilities match the incident requirements.
S103: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays estimated travel times, unit availability, and relevant access constraints.
S104: The Triage Supervisor confirms that the selected response level remains consistent with the caller information.
S105: The selection decision weighs clinical need, travel time, vehicle capability, crew readiness, and regional coverage.
S106: The Fleet Maintenance Cell provides current information about vehicles that are unavailable or restricted.
S107: The Radio Coordinator checks that the proposed unit can be reached on the Regional Radio Network.
S108: A dispatcher may recommend a unit, but dispatch authorization must follow the current regional approval rules.
S109: The Shift Commander approves exceptions that would materially reduce local coverage or require a nonstandard response.
S110: The Regional Medical Director may advise on clinical resource requirements when the incident presents an unusual care need.
S111: The dispatcher records the authorized unit and any conditions attached to its assignment.
S112: Regional Dispatch Center produces the Unit Staging Change Card when a previously selected unit must be repositioned.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
